title: Differentiation under the integral sign: d/dt ∫ g(t⁻¹y) dμ(y) = −t⁻¹·∫ Dg(t⁻¹y)(t⁻¹y) dμ(y)
statement: Let μ be a Borel measure on ℝ^N that is finite on compact sets and let g : ℝ^N → ℝ be a C¹ function with compact support, Dg = fderiv ℝ g. Then for every t > 0 the function r ↦ ∫ g(r⁻¹y) dμ(y) on ℝ (with the convention 0⁻¹ = 0, as in Lean; only its values near t matter) is differentiable at t with derivative −(t⁻¹·∫ Dg(t⁻¹y)(t⁻¹y) dμ(y)).
lean_statement: ∀ (N : ℕ) (μ : Measure (Euclidean N)), IsFiniteMeasureOnCompacts μ → ∀ g : Euclidean N → ℝ, ContDiff ℝ 1 g → HasCompactSupport g → ∀ t : ℝ, 0 < t → HasDerivAt (fun r : ℝ => ∫ y, g (r⁻¹ • y) ∂μ) (-(t⁻¹ * ∫ y, fderiv ℝ g (t⁻¹ • y) (t⁻¹ • y) ∂μ)) t
